diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement lines 33–38 defines omega in {0,1}^d, t_omega=a omega, and law P_omega. The four labels are exactly (0,0)->(0,0), (1,0)->(a,0), (0,1)->(0,a), and (1,1)->(a,a); P_00 etc. are explicitly defined abbreviations. No sample-space arrows or probability-law morphisms are asserted.

Bottom/top horizontal edges connect (0,0) with (1,0) and (0,1) with (1,1), respectively, changing only the first bit. Left/right edges connect (0,0) with (0,1) and (1,0) with (1,1), changing only the second bit. Thus there are four vertices, four distinct undirected edges, and degree two at every vertex, as for the d=2 cube; all four segments are explicit, without cycle syntax.

For fixed j in {0,1}, step 1.1 assigns first-coordinate errors P_(0,j) phi_1 and P_(1,j)(1-phi_1). Step 2.1 bounds their sum below by 1 minus the neighboring TV distance. The statement defines v as the maximum of all neighboring TV distances, so this is at least 1-v with the inequality direction shown. F2 and the cited kernel definition ensure measurable phi_1 with values in [0,1]; F4 and the local TV definition use the event-supremum convention.

Two disjoint horizontal pairs cover all four d=2 vertices, agreeing with 2^(d-1) pairs for i=1 in step 2.1. Thus the picture illustrates the coordinate averaging rather than suggesting one edge proves the whole risk bound. The text leaves the general d-coordinate sum to unchanged step 3.1 and states the rigorous proof is independent.
